routes.speaker: Iain McGilchrist
routes.position: Consciousness is fundamental to reality, and the cosmos's direction, value, and relational character point toward God.

bridges.statement: Fundamental consciousness, cosmic direction, and objective value together support a relational divine ground.
Matter and consciousness are inseparable phases within a wider field of consciousness.
Non-experiential matter cannot explain the arrival of interior experience without leaving the central gap untouched.
Biological and cosmic development display real, open-ended direction rather than fixed engineering.
Beauty, goodness, and truth are discovered features of reality rather than human inventions.
Spiritual experience and ritual can disclose aspects of reality unavailable to reductive description.

routes.speaker: Anil Seth
routes.position: Consciousness is plausibly a biological achievement, while cosmic direction, value, and spirituality do not establish God.

bridges.statement: The discussion does not require primordial consciousness or establish a divine ground.
Consciousness arose through biological evolution and depends intimately on organized living brains.
Precise material and neural research can progressively narrow the explanatory gap.
Thermodynamics, self-organization, and living systems explain apparent direction without divine intention.
Meaning and value grow from living self-maintenance and subsequent evolution.
Spiritual need and experience are real human phenomena without entailing God.
